passage: Hrithik ran the little hardware counter at the bus stand, and the pump repair for old Bhandari's borewell was due by evening. He typed the part details into his phone assistant, and it answered instantly: a half-inch fitting, in a calm, sure tone. He almost cut the pipe. Pankaj, who fixed motors in the next shop, glanced over. "Did it tell you where that came from?" "No. But it sounded certain." Pankaj fetched the maker's booklet and turned to a page. The fitting was three-quarter inch. Hrithik laughed a little, embarrassed, and set the phone down. "So it can be wrong and sound just the same." "Use it to start," Pankaj said. "For anything you can check with a booklet or a tape, check."

qa.q: What fitting size did the assistant give, and what did the booklet show?
qa.a: The assistant said a half-inch fitting, but the booklet showed it was three-quarter inch.

qa.q: Why did Hrithik almost cut the pipe?
qa.a: The answer came instantly in a calm, sure tone, and Hrithik took that certainty as a sign it was right.

qa.q: What should Hrithik do before acting on the assistant's answers in future?
qa.a: Check them against something reliable such as the maker's booklet or a tape, especially when a wrong part would cost time and money.

qa.q: How does Pankaj seem to see the assistant?
qa.a: As a fair place to start, but not an authority. Pankaj checks anything that can be checked against a booklet.

grounding: Fluent, confident AI answers are accepted; Hrithik learns fluency is not accuracy and verifies against a reliable source.

Pranav: dude did you submit the policy report?
Baljeet: yep last night 😎 the AI wrote the references section in like 30 seconds
Pranav: did you check them?
Baljeet: they looked super legit. journal names, page numbers, everything
Pranav: I just searched two of them. they don't exist
Baljeet: what
Pranav: the author exists but that paper doesn't. and the other journal isn't real at all
Baljeet: oh no
Baljeet: it sounded so sure
Pranav: fluent isn't the same as right, bro
Baljeet: I'm emailing the professor now. asking to resubmit with real ones
Pranav: good. I'll help you search the library database tonight
Baljeet: from now on I'm checking every single fact it gives me
Baljeet: facts, numbers, sources. the stuff I can check easily I'll check. the stuff I can't, I won't trust

qa.q: How long did the AI take to write the references section?
What did Baljeet feel when Pranav said the references didn't exist?
qa.a: Baljeet felt shocked and worried, realising the confident answer had fooled them.

qa.q: What did Baljeet decide, and why is it wise?
qa.a: To email the professor and resubmit with real references, and to check every fact, because fluent answers are not always accurate.

qa.q: How does Pranav see Baljeet's trust in the AI?
qa.a: Pranav sees it as too trusting, pointing out that sounding sure isn't the same as being right, but offers help to fix it.

grounding: The chat shows someone accepting fluent, confident AI answers without checking, discovering fake references, and learning to verify facts in proportion to how checkable they are.

passage:
Sumit ran the photocopy and form-filling shop outside the block office in Rewa. Farmers came to him for help with government schemes, and lately he had started asking an AI assistant on his phone for the rules.

On Monday a farmer asked about the crop insurance deadline. The assistant answered in smooth, confident sentences: the fifteenth of next month. Sumit told the farmer to relax.

His friend Sahil, who worked as a clerk inside the block office, stopped by that afternoon. "Who told you the fifteenth? The notice says this Friday."

Sumit's stomach dropped. He had nearly cost a man his season.

He ran to the farmer's village on his cycle before dark and told him the right date. Then he pinned the official notice above his counter.

"The phone talks well," he said to Sahil that night. "But it doesn't carry the stamp. For deadlines, I'll trust the stamp."

qa.a: Outside the block office in Rewa.

qa.q: What did Sumit feel when Sahil told him the real deadline?
qa.a: He felt a sick jolt of fear and guilt, realising he had nearly cost a farmer his season.

qa.q: What did Sumit get right after discovering the error?
qa.a: He cycled to the farmer before dark with the correct date and started relying on the official notice for deadlines.

qa.q: How might the farmer see Sumit's evening visit?
qa.a: The farmer would likely feel relieved and grateful that Sumit came in person to correct the date in time.

grounding: The passage shows someone accepting a fluent, confident AI answer, learning that fluency is not accuracy, and choosing to verify with the official source.
